scope: All four supplied main pages, three figures and 22-reference bibliography. Local SI not located or verified; cited full sources unreviewed.

bibliographic_scope.title: A Solvothermal Route to Nanocrystalline Cu7Te4 at Low Temperature
bibliographic_scope.authors: B. Li; Y. Xie; J. X. Huang; H. L. Su; Y. T. Qian

interpretations.text: The main route uses 7 mmol CuCl2·2H2O and 4 mmol Te in ethylenediamine. The solvent fills 85% of a 100 mL Teflon-lined autoclave before the two solids are added successively. A sealed 160 °C treatment for 10 h, natural cooling, filtration, water/ethanol washing and vacuum drying at 60 °C for 4 h produce the specimen characterized in Figures 1–3.

interpretations.topic: Phase, crystallite size and particle diameter
interpretations.text: Figure 1 indexes hexagonal Cu7Te4 with a = 8.335 Å and c = 7.211 Å, close to JCPDS 18-456. The source estimates a crystallite size of about 15 nm by the Scherrer formula. Figure 3 separately shows homogeneous nanoparticles with an average TEM diameter near 15 nm. These two approximate estimates use different methods and do not establish a measured coordinate model or a particle-size distribution.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figures 1 and 3 and accompanying analysis

interpretations.topic: XPS composition and a printed unit anomaly
interpretations.text: The reported Cu 2p and Te 3d peak positions are 932.4 eV and 572.7 eV. Peak quantification gives Cu:Te = 63.41:36.29; this ratio is retained without renormalization. The printed charge reference is C 1s at 284.60 kV, although specimen peaks and plotted axes use eV. That unit anomaly remains unresolved. The source reports no obvious oxide peaks but provides no impurity detection limit.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 2–3, Figure 2 and XPS discussion

interpretations.text: Benzene and diethylamine comparisons did not react tellurium with copper chloride. The authors propose that polar, bidentate ethylenediamine stabilizes metal-polytellurido intermediates and promotes dissolution, diffusion and crystallization while absorbing reaction heat. They compare quoted solvent critical temperatures of 318 °C for ethylenediamine and 374 °C for water. These are explanatory source context, not measured synthesis temperatures or identified intermediates.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3, Solvent and reaction-mechanism discussion

interpretations.text: A 3:2 copper-salt/Te feed gives Cu7Te4 mixed with unreacted tellurium rather than the expected Cu3Te2. A 2:1 feed gives only hexagonal Cu7Te4 rather than Cu2Te. Replacing CuCl2 with CuI also gives Cu7Te4 nanoparticles. The source does not separately assign absolute charges, complete conditions, particle sizes or displayed figures to these comparisons; they remain supporting contexts.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3, Molar-ratio and CuI substitution paragraph

interpretations.topic: An unresolved intermediate and further heating
interpretations.text: At 140 °C an XRD-observed intermediate could not be identified against the available JCPDS patterns. Its assignment as a Cu/Te/ethylenediamine complex is the authors’ inference. Further heating of this intermediate at 180 °C produces Cu7Te4 described as pure, with no treatment time or numerical purity limit supplied. Below 120 °C, neither the intermediate nor reacted tellurium is reported. The 180 °C context retains explicit lineage from the 140 °C intermediate without inventing its formula or handling.

evidence.locator: Main PDF p. 3, Temperature-dependent intermediate discussion

interpretations.topic: Application motivation is not a measured property
interpretations.text: The introduction discusses thermoelectric applications, thermopower, electrical resistivity and thermal conductivity using cited literature. No numerical thermoelectric property is measured on these Cu7Te4 powders. Cited full papers remain unreviewed and do not supply missing experimental conditions.

source_conflicts: The printed XPS charge reference is C 1s at 284.60 kV, while the reported specimen peaks and plotted axes use eV. This source unit anomaly is retained, not silently corrected or used in a calculation.
limitations: Complete four-page supplied main only; no matching local SI located or verified. Cited full papers remain unreviewed.
Reagent purities, heating ramp, measured autoclave pressure, agitation, cooling rate, filter medium, wash volumes/repetition count and vacuum pressure are unreported.

The main method supplies 7 mmol copper chloride dihydrate and 4 mmol Te, a 100 mL vessel, 85% solvent filling, 160 °C for 10 h and vacuum drying at 60 °C for 4 h. The solvent volume is not separately printed as mL and is not silently converted.

Eight comparison contexts preserve solvent, ratio, precursor and temperature changes. Their absolute charges and complete temperature/dwell/workup assignments are not separately stated; they do not inherit the quantified main specimen or its figures and measurements.

XRD crystallite size and TEM diameter are separate approximate estimates. Lattice constants are indexed specimen parameters, not atomic coordinates; no exact unit-cell or particle-coordinate model is supplied.
